# Novaplan AI

> Documentation for Novaplan AI workspaces: connected company knowledge, search, cited answers, and agents.

Novaplan AI is a closed-source product. Novaplan creates customer workspaces and invites users. Use an existing workspace; do not direct customers to install or deploy the platform. Setup responsibilities and available administrator or developer features must be confirmed with Novaplan.

For existing-workspace support, use support@novaplan.ai. The contact form at https://www.novaplan.ai/contact is for sales and demo enquiries.

Novaplan manages most setup and administration. The full reference remains available. Both German and English documentation are being maintained; the German translation is in progress and currently covers the priority guides below. Do not describe the full reference as already translated.

## Customer guides

- [Introduction](https://docs.novaplan.ai/introduction.md): Product overview.
- [Getting started](https://docs.novaplan.ai/quickstart.md): Invitations and workspace sign-in.
- [Support](https://docs.novaplan.ai/contact-us.md): Help with an existing workspace.
- [FAQ](https://docs.novaplan.ai/additional-resources/faq.md): Access and setup responsibilities.
- [Connectors overview](https://docs.novaplan.ai/connectors/overview.md): Reference for connected sources.
- [Agents overview](https://docs.novaplan.ai/agent-guide/overview.md): Agent concepts and configuration.

## Administrator and integration reference

- [Onboarding](https://docs.novaplan.ai/onboarding.md): Settings for the administrator responsible for the agreed setup.
- [Developer access](https://docs.novaplan.ai/developer/getting-started.md): Integration reference and access requirements.
- [MCP overview](https://docs.novaplan.ai/mcp/overview.md): Connecting compatible clients to an existing workspace.
- [Personal access tokens](https://docs.novaplan.ai/developer/personal-access-tokens.md): User-scoped authentication.
- [OAuth 2.0](https://docs.novaplan.ai/developer/oauth2.md): Application authorization.

Technical package names, API paths, scopes, and environment variables can retain upstream identifiers. Do not rename them merely for branding. Never expose credentials or tokens in chat or logs.
